# The encoding question this file used to carry is now settled by measurement. Unity
# 2022.3 spells m_LayerCollisionMatrix as 256 hex chars = 32 chunks of 8, chunk k
# describing layer k, each chunk the uint32 mask written as its LITTLE-ENDIAN BYTES
# (0x000041ea -> "ea410000"). That is what the menu left in the file: the string now on
# disk is byte-identical to the little-endian candidate at the bottom of this file, and
# decoding it by that reading reproduces all 32 mask_dec values below. The big-endian
# digits reading reproduces 5 of 32, and those 5 are exactly the layers whose mask is
# all-ones -- the only spelling-invariant value, which is why a wrong reading can look
# partly right. A wrong reading still parses without an error, which is why this field
# The route that sidesteps the encoding entirely: Physics.IgnoreLayerCollision(i, j,
# ignore) is the only public per-pair setter (verified against UnityEngine.PhysicsModule.xml;
# there is no Physics.SetLayerCollision), and Unity serialises the result itself. Verify
# by reading the 256 chars back and decoding to 32 uint32 against the mask_dec column.
# Physics.GetIgnoreLayerCollision(a, b) observes Unity's own decoded result, and symmetry

# Two facts only the run could establish: the write does land in ProjectSettings/

# 26 of the 32 layers must not collide with themselves, and the written file has those
